title: Transdiagnostic mechanisms in maltreatment-associated psychopathology in adolescents: Investigating inflammatory and regulatory flexibility
summary:
Experiences of childhood maltreatment represent a significant and well-established risk factor for the development of various mental disorders. Current research suggests that this relationship may be jointly mediated by two key factors: flexible emotion regulation and inflammatory activity. Flexible emotion regulation describes the ability to modulate emotions appropriately to the situation and represents a protective transdiagnostic factor for mental health. Previous research findings have already shown that the ability of flexible emotion regulation can be impaired as a result of maltreatment experiences in childhood.
Inflammatory activity describes inflammatory processes in terms of inflammation parameters in the blood following abuse or other traumatic experiences, which are closely associated with the development and maintenance of psychopathology.
This study aims to comprehensively investigate the role of flexible emotion regulation and inflammatory activity in the interplay between childhood maltreatment and psychopathology in a high-risk cohort of adolescents receiving treatment in child and adolescent psychiatry. For the first time in a longitudinal study, the timing and type of maltreatment experiences will be considered while simultaneously examining the interactions between emotion regulation and inflammatory mechanisms.
In addition to analyzing inflammatory markers and conducting psychological assessments, the study employs the method of Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) to measure flexible emotion regulation. EMA enables the real-time and context-sensitive assessment of emotion regulation as a dynamic process in everyday situations.
The overarching goal of the study is to gain fundamental insights into the mechanisms underlying the development of psychopathology following childhood maltreatment. These insights could contribute to improving therapeutic interventions for adolescents with a history of maltreatment.
EmoFlexImmun is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG).
conditions: Emotion regulation and inflammation in the link between child maltreatment and mental disorders in inpatients and outpatients undergoing psychiatric or psychotherapeutic treatment

interventions.name:
Adolescents with a history of child maltreatment and adolescents without a history of child maltreatment who are undergoing treatment for psychiatric/psychological symptoms.

In this study arm, systematic assessments will be conducted at two defined time points for all participants:

Time Point

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria Patients with a history of child maltreatment:
(1) In inpatient or outpatient treatment for various psychiatric or psychological symptoms
(2) Experience of child maltreatment
(3) Age between 13 and 17 years
(4) Sufficient knowledge of the German language 
(5) Availability of the signed declaration of consent (patient, if necessary legal guardian)
(6) Own smartphone

Inclusion criteria Patients without a history of child maltreatment:
(1) In inpatient or outpatient treatment for various psychiatric or psychological symptoms 
(2) No history of child maltreatment (but potentially other traumatic experiences)
(3) Age between 13 and 17 years
(4) Sufficient knowledge of the German language
(5) No permanent medication with antidepressants or antipsychotics
(6) No intake of systemic corticosteroids within the last 2 months
(7) No acute physical illnesses
(8) No fever in the last seven days
(9) No other severe symptoms indicating activation or suppression of the immune system (example: purulent sputum, congenital or acquired immunodeficiency)
(10) Availability of the signed declaration of consent (patient, if necessary legal guardian)
(11) Own smartphone
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria Patients with a history of child maltreatment:
(1) Fixed medication with antidepressants or antipsychotics 
(2) Intake of systemic corticosteroids within the last 2 months
(3) Acute physical illnesses (e.g. injuries)
(4) Fever in the last seven days
(5) Other severe symptoms indicating activation or suppression of the immune system (e.g. purulent   sputum, congenital or acquired immunodeficiency)
